New recheck workflow itself remains unexecuted until draft publication.

U2.detail: Freeze SHA256SUMS rechecked with zero failures; worktree exact commit/tree clean; parent recorded 126 focused + 551 existing tests, workflow syntax, precommit, gitleaks, L3 change-contract and diff check PASS.

U3.detail: Live main protection requires Security Review, Documentation Check, identity-check, Unit Tests, CodeQL language checks, CI Pipeline Summary, independent embedded audit, and PR Steward / final readiness. required_status_checks.strict=true.

U4.detail: Executed-proof base-SHA enforcement is pre-existing and outside this packet allowlist. Current main equals audited base. Publication/reuse must reharvest on base movement; separate L3 follow-up should enforce executed proof base_sha directly.

risk_dispositions.detail: Candidate collection requires run.status == 'completed' before an artifact is considered (trusted_run with successful=False). If the newest trusted embedded-audit run for the exact head failed and is then re-run (status in_progress, prior-attempt artifact still listed), that run is skipped as untrusted and the next-newest completed run — possibly an older green — is selected and dispatched. This is spec-conformant ('trusted completed') and test_newer_untrusted_run_is_not_considered[status=in_progress] enshrines it. The window is transient and self-correcting: when the re-run completes, pr-steward.yml's own workflow_run trigger on embedded-audit completion re-publishes from the newest run, and Steward re-verifies proof bytes and live head. Not attacker-mintable without write access.
risk_dispositions.title: In-progress re-run attempt of a newer failed trusted audit opens a transient older-green window

risk_dispositions.detail: Selection enumerates exact-name artifacts, not audit runs. A newer trusted audit run that failed before its upload step (or whose artifact expired/was deleted) contributes no candidate, so an older green artifact would be selected. Bounded: embedded-audit uploads with if: always()/if-no-files-found: error, and Steward cannot publish any commit status without a downloaded PROOF.json (publish step gated on steps.proof.outputs.head_sha), so no red status exists to be resurrected over in that case. No run_attempt/run_started_at binding is done in the recheck; Steward's per-run exact-single-artifact selector fails closed on duplicates.
risk_dispositions.title: Newer-red dominance is artifact-keyed; artifact-less or expired newer failed runs are invisible

risk_dispositions.detail: Steward binds live head and base from one live PR read and passes expected_base_sha to enforce_independent_audit_proof. However independent_audit_errors applies expected_base_sha only on the not-required (L0/L1) branch via _not_required_proof_errors/contract binding, and verify_workflow_artifact (which checks provenance.change_contract.base_sha == expected_base_sha) is only invoked by pr-steward.yml when embedded_audit.required is False. For L2/L3 executed proofs, a proof classified at base B1 can be reused by a review-triggered Steward run after main advanced to B2 without failing closed at Steward. Head binding is fully enforced at every layer (artifact name, PROOF head_sha, live head, pre-dispatch re-check). Downstream, verify_pr_steward_readiness_artifact requires receipt.base_sha == live PR base at merge time, so base drift after the Steward run still fails closed. This is pre-existing unchanged-context behaviour, not introduced by the candidate, but the candidate makes the drift window reachable in practice (previously ready_for_review re-audited at current base). A follow-on should enforce contract.base_sha for executed proofs too.
risk_dispositions.title: Base-SHA binding of reused executed (model-required) proofs is not enforced inline by Steward; evidence reuse widens the audit-to-Steward base-drift window

risk_dispositions.detail: Per GitHub semantics (not verifiable from INPUT), pull_request_review runs the workflow file from the PR merge ref and, for fork PRs, with a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN. Consequences: (a) a same-repo PR author with write access could alter pr-steward-recheck.yml in their branch and exercise actions:write — no escalation beyond what write access already grants (manual dispatch of pr-steward.yml), no secrets beyond github.token, and Steward independently re-validates run identity, proof bytes and live head; (b) ordinary reviews on fork PRs make the dispatch POST fail 403 -> red recheck run (fail closed, noisy); fork PR readiness relies on ready_for_review (pull_request_target, base context) or manual dispatch.
risk_dispositions.title: pull_request_review execution context: PR-merge-ref workflow definition for same-repo PRs; read-only token for fork PRs

risk_dispositions.detail: Recheck concurrency cancels only rechecks per PR. pr-steward.yml (unchanged) is triggered both by embedded-audit completion and by recheck dispatch, and publishes the readiness status with last-writer-wins. Two Steward runs harvesting live review state seconds apart could finish out of order. Pre-existing; the candidate increases Steward trigger frequency (every review submitted/dismissed, every ready_for_review, every green PR CI completion).
risk_dispositions.title: Steward has no concurrency group; recheck-dispatched and audit-completion Steward runs for the same head can interleave (status last-writer-wins)

risk_dispositions.detail: Every Complete-CI completion (push to main, merge_group, dispatch) now produces a cheap green RECHECK_NOOP run (repaired from red). A successful PR CI completion that lands before embedded-audit has uploaded its artifact yields RECHECK_BLOCKED ('no reusable trusted audit artifact'), a red run in the Actions tab that is not attached to the PR; the subsequent audit completion triggers Steward directly, so readiness is not lost. gemini-dispatch.yml (unchanged, out of scope) still starts a run on every review submitted whose dispatch job is skipped by the @gemini-cli + collaborator + sender=User gate; model spend is zero.
risk_dispositions.title: Residual trigger noise: recheck run per Complete-CI completion and red recheck when PR CI finishes before the audit artifact exists; gemini-dispatch skipped-job runs persist

risk_dispositions.detail: The script relies on gh --paginate --slurp (gh >= 2.45), the GITHUB_REPOSITORY_ID default env var, and datetime.fromisoformat accepting '+00:00' offsets (Python >= 3.11). Absence of any yields CalledProcessError/KeyError/ValueError -> job failure with no dispatch, silently disabling reuse until fixed.
risk_dispositions.title: Runner/tooling assumptions fail closed but untested live

risk_dispositions.detail: Tests do exec the actual inline script from the YAML with only subprocess.run replaced, and cover A/B/C plus stale/wrong-head/failed/expired/ambiguous/API-error/race cases; the RED log proves the A/B/C tests fail against H1. Limits: the gemini gate test re-implements the Actions expression engine in Python (non-authoritative); execute() catches only SystemExit/ValueError/CalledProcessError, so KeyError/TypeError shapes (e.g. an artifact with name None reaching PROOF_NAME.fullmatch) are not characterised, though they fail closed via traceback; the 126/551 pass counts are operator-recorded, not re-executed here.
risk_dispositions.title: Test limits: expression-engine emulation, uncharacterised exception classes, no live execution
